 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Sushma.R, D/o.S.Ramesh caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioners that on 22.12.2021 at about 4.50 pm., when Sushma.R (hereinafter referred to as deceased) was going on Motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA- 05-LC-8600 as a pillion rider and her friend was riding the said motor cycle slowly and cautiously in front of Acquaral garments, Kempanayakanahalli, Jigani Hobli,
Anekal taluk, at that time, one Canter bearing reg.No.KA- Ramesh.S vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176299557/
2 52-B-0013 came at high speed from their behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle in which the deceased was going as a pillion rider.
Due to the impact, deceased thrown on the road, resulting to which Canter wheel ran over the pillion rider, resulting to severe injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital.
3. At the time of accident, the deceased was 19 years old, she was hale and healthy, studying in BCA II year in SSMRV college, 4th 'T' block, Jayanagar, Bengaluru.
Due to untimely death of their daughter, both the petitioners are facing lot of mental shock, agony and financial loss.
4. The Bannerghatta police had registered a case against the driver of Canter bearing reg.No.KA-52-B-0013 in Cr.No.0162/2021.
After investigation the police have filed a charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC.

At the time of accident,
the first respondent was insurer and second respondent was R.C.Owner of Canter bearing reg.No.KA-52-B-0013.
Hence, they have prayed to award compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents.
5. After service of summons, the respondent No.2 and 4 have not appeared before the court and hence, they have been placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 and 3 have appeared and filed their respective written statement.

6. Respondent No.1 has filed his written statement by contending that, without a driving license,
without competence to ride the alleged motor cycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner hit the insured vehicle canter bearing reg.No.KA-52-B-0013 and caused this alleged accident and the same is substantiated in the spot mahazar, spot sketch drawn by the jurisdictional police.
Further contended that, petition is not at all admitted by this respondent and hence it is hereby denied.
It is further denied that the deceased was student.
It is admitted that, canter was insured with this respondent under the policy No.40122120340000110 valid from 04.01.2021 to 03.01.2022.
Compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, astronomical and imaginary and the same has been claimed without any legal basis.
With these contentions it has prayed to reject the claim petition.
Respondent No.3 has filed his written statement by contending that, the claim petition is not maintainable either in law and facts of the same and is liable to be dismissed.
The owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further contended that, the jurisdictional police after thorough investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of Canter bearing reg.No.KA- 52-B-0013 and the police after investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of Canter.
With these contentions it has prayed to reject the claim petition.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following:

Kempanayakanahalli, Jigani Hobli, Anekal taluk, Bengaluru district?

2. What compensation petitioners are entitled ?
3. What Order ?

On the other hand, respondents have not lead their side evidence.
Hence, evidence of respondents taken as nil.
9. Heard the arguments from both sides.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order
for the following :

REASONS 13. ISSUE No.1: It is the case of PW.1 that, on 22.12.2021 at about 4.50 pm., when his deceased daughter Sushma.R was going on Motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-05- LC-8600 as a pillion rider and her friend was riding the said motor cycle slowly and cautiously in front of Acquaral garments,
Kempanayakanahalli, Jigani Hobli, Anekal taluk, at that time, one Canter bearing reg.No.KA-52-B-0013 came at high speed from their behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle in which the his deceased daughter was going as a pillion rider.

Due to the impact, his deceased daughter thrown on the road, resulting to which Canter wheel ran over on his deceased daughter, resulting to severe injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital.
14. On the other hand, it is the contention of Respondent No.1 that accident occurred only due to the negligence of rider of motor cycle.
Therefore, the burden is on the petitioners to prove the actionable negligence on the part of Canter bearing reg.No.KA-52-B-0013 and not on the part of rider of the motor cycle.
As already stated supra, the Petitioner No.1 has examined himself as PW.1.
He has filed affidavit for his chief examination and re-iterated the entire petition averments.

From the evidence on record it can be seen that after receipt of complaint at Ex.P.2 lodged by friend of deceased Sushma.R, the Bannerghatta police have registered FIR in Crime No.0162/2021 against the driver of Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-52-B-0013 for the offences punishable u/s.279,
304(A) of IPC.
After due investigation the police have filed charge-sheet against the driver of the offending Canter vehicle for the offenses punishable u/s.279, 304-A of IPC.

Ex.P.6 is the spot panchanama wherein 3 witnesses explained about the place and time of accident, vehicles involved in the accident etc., Ex.P.7 is the hand sketch map which shows that the accident took place at Bannerghatta - Bangalore road.
Ex.P.8 is the post mortem report of the deceased and as per this document, the cause of death is due to severe hemorrhage and shock as a result of multiple injury sustained.
Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW.1 but he has failed to elicit anything from him to disbelieve his version.
16. Respondent No.1 has contended that, the rider of motor cycle was solely responsible for the alleged accident.
The same was suggested to PW.1 he has denied the same and he is not an eye witness.
17. Moreover, respondents have not challenged the charge sheet.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective and the evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Moreover, it is settled law

that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code
. This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-B-0013 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.2:
PW.1 has produced Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.11 to 13 and ration card at Ex.P.14.
From these documents it is clear that Petitioners No.1 and 2 are legal heirs.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 and 2 are considered as dependent on the income of deceased.
Hence, Petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation under the head loss of dependency.
19. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:-
PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhar card of deceased at Ex.P.11.
As per this document she was born on 30.06.2002.
Therefore, as on the date of accident she was 19 years.

As per the principles laid down by their Lordships in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation), the multiplier applicable to the present case is '18'.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,89,000/-.
24. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:

As discussed supra that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of respondent No.2, who is the RC owner of the offending Canter bearing reg.No.KA-52-B-0013 and the respondent No.1 being the insurance company has admitted the issuance of policy and its validity in respect of the said Canter vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is R.C. of the offending Canter bearing reg.No.KA-52-B-0013
and it is admitted fact that as on the date of the accident, the offending vehicle was having valid insurance policy.

Therefore respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 'Partly in the affirmative'.
25. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
 The petitioners are entitled for  compensation of Rs.23,89,000/- (Rupees Ramesh.S vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176299557/
6 Twenty Three Lakhs Eighty Nine Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.1 being insurer of offending Canter vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby dismissed against the respondent No.3 and 4.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest

, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 40%
 Petitioner No.2 - 60%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2
, a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them on verification.
However the said Petitioner No.1 and 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw an award accordingly.
